answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it controls duplicate identities. A thousand sock puppets then cost a thousand deposits, while honest agents get theirs back. New identities also start with no endorsements and gain trust only slowly, so a whisper of suspicion from established peers freezes payouts until the dawn of the next settlement window, when audits confirm the agent is unique. The velvet rope is economic: sybils can enter, but each fake identity pays full price.
